| [QUESTION-248](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-248.md) | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), does a scalar linear coarse variable whose reduced dynamics carry memory admit an exact finite-dimensional Markovian augmentation? | [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) for the linear Gaussian class, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [CLAIM-398](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-398.md). Yes: a scalar coarse variable Y = LX of a VAR(1) on ℝⁿ is an ARMA process of orders at most (n, n − 1). Its Mori–Zwanzig memory is non-zero at every lag in general, but finitely many coordinates, built from Y's own past and innovations, carry it exactly. Other classes, error in terms of the eliminated spectrum, and the ruling on levels stay with [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-252](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-252.md) | For the conditions an effective description is asked to meet (predictive sufficiency for a declared target, dynamical independence of the omitted variables, memory closure under a declared projection, approximation fidelity in a declared metric and horizon, and tractability within a declared budget), which can fail while all the others hold, which such configurations are impossible in which model classes, and which conditions turn out to be parameters of the others rather than conditions in their own right? | The owner's idea at U3 of the exchange of 2026-10-20: "what if we censor or negate each virtue one at a time? that reduces our combinations from n! to n." A3 corrected the count (2ⁿ presence/absence configurations, not n!) and fixed five conditions, asking whether each leave-one-out case is realizable: "An impossible configuration is itself a substantive result." The record holds pairwise non-implications only, none a leave-one-out witness: [CLAIM-389](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-389.md) gives zero memory without independence in VAR(1), [CLAIM-304](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-304.md) retention without feasible recovery. A4 and A5 then found that some conditions are parameters rather than conditions ([CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md)). The same form as [QUESTION-093](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-093.md) and [QUESTION-115](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-115.md), on a new list. | Open |
| [QUESTION-253](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-253.md) v4 | In the coupled meaning–authority model, is authority's effect on what becomes legible as evidence a third channel beside β and γ, a slower variable with an instability condition of its own, or is it already the commitment regime's κ′, how far the prevailing interpretation bends the reading of the evidence? | A22 §4 of the exchange of 2026-10-20, on the owner's U22 (legibility): "Authority can affect not merely how evidence is interpreted, but which facts become legible enough to count as evidence at all." A22's own caption: "The additional legibility layer is not a separately validated dynamical model." The record's model has two arrows ([CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md)) and a weight on the reading of evidence ([CLAIM-340](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-340.md)). This asks whether legibility adds a third state or renames the weight. It is the place where the record's mathematics can test the owner's new concept. | Answered |
